title: Latent effector capacity governs reversible T cell exhaustion: A theoretical mathematical model of PD-1 blockade response.
authors: Liew, Aubrey Y; Li, Ying; Dong, Haidong
one_liner_zh: 该文提出T细胞耗竭的理论数学模型，虽涉及表观遗传可及性，但对象为免疫细胞状态而非染色质三维组织，且无AI或分子模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: T cell exhaustion is often viewed as a terminal state marked by irreversible loss of function during chronic infection and cancer. However, the rapid recovery of antitumor activity in clinical responders after PD-1 blockade suggests that some exhausted T cells retain hidden functional potential. To explain this paradox, we present a theoretical framework that separates latent effector capacity from active effector function. Latent effector capacity represents a history-dependent state reflecting preserved epigenetic accessibility and regulatory readiness, distinct from ongoing gene expression. In this model, PD-1 signaling acts as a reversible mask that suppresses effector function without eliminating the underlying effector capacity. The framework explains preserved chromatin accessibility, rapid reinvigoration after checkpoint blockade, and variable therapeutic responses. By incorporating nonlinear maintenance and erosion of latent effector capacity, the model predicts a bistable system with a point of no return beyond which exhaustion becomes irreversible. These principles may guide development of mechanistically informed biomarkers and artificial intelligence models predicting response to PD-1 therapy.
abstract_zh: T细胞耗竭通常被视为一种终末状态，以慢性感染和癌症中功能不可逆丧失为特征。然而，临床应答者在PD-1阻断后抗肿瘤活性的快速恢复表明，部分耗竭T细胞保留了隐藏的功能潜力。为解释这一悖论，我们提出一个理论框架，将潜在效应能力与活跃效应功能区分开来。潜在效应能力代表一种依赖于历史的状态，反映保留的表观遗传可及性和调控准备状态，区别于持续进行的基因表达。在该模型中，PD-1信号充当一种可逆掩蔽，抑制效应功能而不消除潜在的效应能力。该框架解释了保留的染色质可及性、检查点阻断后的快速恢复以及多变的治疗反应。通过纳入潜在效应能力的非线性维持和侵蚀，该模型预测了一个双稳态系统，其存在一个不可逆点，超过该点耗竭变得不可逆。这些原则可能指导基于机制的生物标志物和预测PD-1治疗反应的人工智能模型的发展。
